replies.raw:
Last time, you learned the postcard rule.

AI can copy someone's voice from a short recording — even a video posted online. Scammers use that to call you sounding exactly like a grandchild or other relative.

Even if their name or number shows on your screen, callers can fake that too.

Here are the warning signs, one at a time:

- It's urgent.
- It's a secret ("don't tell Mom").
- They want cash, gift cards, or money sent from your bank.
- Some even send someone to your door to pick up cash.

[EX]In 2023, an Arizona mother got a call. Her 15-year-old daughter was safe the whole time. But a voice that sounded exactly like her daughter asked for help, and a man demanded money. The mother later told the U.S. Senate about it.[/EX]

A code word is a word only your family knows. If a caller can't say it, hang up.
